chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who prays the voluntary prayers in the cities, while he is upon his riding animal, facing wherever it turns him, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem.'

key_terms.الْأَمْصَارِ: Cities or urban areas (distinct from open desert/travel)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray voluntary prayers while riding an animal in the city?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kāfī clarifies that the concession for praying nafl while mounted applies even within settled urban areas (al-amṣār), not exclusively during long journeys, emphasizing the ease (rukhas) granted to the believer. It underscores the Shia juristic principle that the animal's natural orientation suffices for the qibla direction when a rider is mounted, reflecting the practical flexibility of the Imams in ritual law. This ruling is often cited in discussions regarding the distinction between obligatory (fard) and voluntary (nafl) prayers regarding the necessity of facing the qibla precisely.
